available-plugins get.help:
Lists the Oracle Cloud Agent plugins that are available for compute instances. 
[Command Reference](listInstanceagentAvailablePlugins)

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment. [required]

params.name: os_name
params.help:
The image (OS) for the compute instance.

If no match is found, all plugins are returned.

Examples: `CentOS`, `Oracle Linux`, `Oracle Autonomous Linux`, `Canonical Ubuntu`, `Windows Server` [required]

params.name: os_version
params.help:
The OS version for the instance.

If no match is found, all plugins are returned.

Examples: `7.9`, `8` for CentOS and Oracle Linux. `20.04`, `20.04 Minimal` for Canonical Ubuntu. `2012 R2 Datacenter`, `2019 Standard` for Windows Server. [required]

params.name: page
params.help: For list pagination. The value of the `opc-next-page` response header from the previous "List" call. For important details about how pagination works, see [List Pagination].

params.name: limit
params.help: For list pagination. The maximum number of results per page, or items to return in a paginated "List" call. For important details about how pagination works, see [List Pagination].

params.name: sort_by
params.help:
The field to sort by. You can provide one sort order (`sortOrder`). Default order for `TIMECREATED` is descending.

**Note:** In general, some "List" operations (for example, `ListInstances`) let you optionally filter by availability domain if the scope of the resource type is within a single availability domain. If you call one of these "List" operations without specifying an availability domain, the resources are grouped by availability domain, then sorted.

params.name: sort_order
params.help: The sort order to use, either ascending (`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`). The `DISPLAYNAME` sort order is case sensitive.

params.name: name
params.help: The plugin name.

params.name: all_pages
params.help: Fetches all pages of results. If you provide this option, then you cannot provide the --limit option.

params.name: page_size
params.help: When fetching results, the number of results to fetch per call. Only valid when used with --all or --limit, and ignored otherwise.

command cancel.help:
Cancels a command that is scheduled to run on a compute instance that is managed by Oracle Cloud Agent.

Canceling a command is a best-effort attempt. If the command has already completed, it will not be canceled. 
[Command Reference](cancelInstanceAgentCommand)

params.name: if_match
params.help: For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource.  The resource will be updated or deleted only if the etag you provide matches the resource's current etag value.

params.help: Perform deletion without prompting for confirmation.

command create.help:
Creates a command or script to run on a compute instance that is managed by Oracle Cloud Agent.

On Linux instances, the script runs in a bash shell. On Windows instances, the script runs in a batch shell.

Commands that require administrator privileges will run only if Oracle Cloud Agent is running with administrator privileges. 
[Command Reference](createInstanceAgentCommand)

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment to create the command in. [required]

params.name: target
params.help:
The target instance to run the command on.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.
 [required]

params.name: content
params.help:
The contents of the command.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.
 [required]

params.name: display_name
params.help:
A user-friendly name for the command. It does not have to be unique. Avoid entering confidential information.

Example: `Database Backup Script`

params.name: timeout_in_seconds
params.help: Command execution time limit. Zero means no timeout. [required]
